title: TF versioning signal and deprecation runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick operational runbook to surface, signal, and execute deprecation and breaking-change rollouts for Terraform modules used in Private deployments (VPC + on-prem packages). This is intentionally pragmatic — a mixture of checks, thresholds, and communication templates we can iterate on.

Scope: applies to all Terraform modules published to our internal module registry under registry.redwood.internal/private-deployments/* including: network, kube-bootstrap, external-secrets, logging-agent, vm-image, and RBAC modules. Excludes ephemeral demo modules.

Principles (short):
- Signal early: prefer conservative deprecation windows and automated detection of consumers.
- Make upgrades low-friction: provide example upgrade snippets + migration helpers.
- Safety first: staged canary -> regional rollout -> global release.
- Observable rollback: every release must include a rollback tag and quick revert path.

Semantic versioning policy (operational summary):
- MAJOR (X.y.z): incompatible API changes (resource renames, removal of outputs, change of module variable semantics) -> requires deprecation proposal, 90-day notice, and explicit migration guide.
- MINOR (x.Y.z): new backwards-compatible features (new optional variables, new outputs) -> announce, default to disabled or harmless defaults, 14-day notice recommended.
- PATCH (x.y.Z): bug fixes, docs, tests -> publish with changelog, no notice required beyond registry change log.

Signal and detection system (how we know there are consumers and impact):
1) Registry consumer mapping: maintain subscribers.csv (automatically generated by registry hooks) listing consumer repo, last seen apply date, terraform version.
2) Telemetry: on module install artifact (CI hook) we capture module version and workspace id (anonymized). Build a weekly report: top-50 modules by active workspaces.
3) GitHub dependency sweep: scheduled GH action scans terraform lockfiles and module sources to find pinned versions.
4) Plan failure watch: our SRE CI job forwards terraform plan errors referencing module IDs to a digest.

Deprecation decision workflow (short):
- Trigger: proposers (module owner) files a deprecation proposal (Confluence + JIRA ticket).
- Review: internal module guild (owners + infra + security) reviews impact matrix and migration effort.
- Notification window: MAJOR change -> 90 days; MINOR change -> 14 days; emergency -> as soon as possible with rollback plan.
- Approvals: module owner + infra eng manager signoff required.

Communications checklist (templates below):
- Registry changelog entry (always).
- Email to consumer list + slack #private-deployments with TL;DR and migration link.
- Optional: schedule migration open office hours (30–60 mins) within first 2 weeks for MAJOR changes.

Rollout strategy (recommended):
1) Canary group: pick 2–4 non-critical customers or an internal staging cluster. Apply module update via PR automation. Monitor 72 hours.
2) Regional ramp: enable for one region / datacenter range for 7 days.
3) Full: after metrics look green, release to all.
Rollback policy: publish a rollback-tag (x.y-rollback) with the previous working state. Rollback must be executable via single PR to module consumer repos created by our automation (registry-bot).

Metrics to monitor (must be in dashboards for any MAJOR release):
- Plan failures referencing module path (count / hour)
- Apply success rate by workspace (rate 24h rolling)
- Time-to-complete applies (95th percentile)
- Incidents created in 72h after release (count)
- Customer-reported regressions (Slack/Jira mentions)

Automations and tests required before publish:
- Module-level unit tests (terraform validate & fmt) in CI (required).
- Integration smoke tests: apply -> plan -> apply -> destroy against minimal infra (required for MAJOR).
- Backcompat matrix: run with each supported terraform minor (e.g., 1.4.x, 1.5.x) when changing provider usage.
- Registry pre-publish hook: verifies changelog, semver tag, migration notes file present.

Registry publishing checklist (pre-publish):
- Update CHANGELOG.md with high-level notes and example migration snippet.
- Add MIGRATION.md for MAJOR changes with step-by-step patching.
- Add automated test job names in registry manifest.
- Tag repo (git tag x.y.z) and push. Registry-bot will: sign tag, generate release notes, update subscribers.csv.
- If MAJOR: create deprecation JIRA and customer notification draft.

Breaking-change detection example (internal script):
- run: scripts/find-consumers.sh --module network/v2 --threshold 3d
- output: consumer list + last-apply + severity score (how many resources reference removed outputs)

Migration snippet examples (to include in MIGRATION.md):
- Old variable change: variable "enable_ipv6" (bool -> string)
  -> Recommend: introduce new variable enable_ipv6_mode = "disabled" | "auto"; provide compatibility layer: if var.enable_ipv6 != null ? var.enable_ipv6 : (var.enable_ipv6_mode == "auto" ? true : false)
- Output rename: old output "subnet_id" -> new output "public_subnet_id". Provide a compatibility output: public_subnet_id = try(module.network.public_subnet_id, module.network.subnet_id)

Communication templates (short):
- Slack/Email subject: [module:network] Breaking change planned (v2.0.0) — action required
- Body: TL;DR what changed, why, who to contact, migration link, timeline, failing plan example, optional automated PR link.

Quick onboarding for module owners (steps):
1) Open a deprecation proposal doc (confluence template exists).
2) Run consumer-scan and attach results.
3) Draft MIGRATION.md + minimal sample upgrade PR.
4) Create a staging release and run canary automation.
5) Open office hours if >5 subscribers or strategic accounts.

Unresolved / TODO (to iterate in next revision):
- Define exact severity scoring formula for breaking changes (currently ad-hoc).
- Hook registry telemetry into Datadog dashboard for automated alerting on plan failures.
- Standardize automation for creating consumer PRs and opt-out flags.

Appendix: useful commands and examples
- Find consumers via GH action artifact: gh workflow run consumer-scan.yml --repo registry --ref main
- Local consumer scan script: ./scripts/find-consumers.sh --module "modules/network" --days 30 > consumers-30d.csv
- Trigger canary rollout: ./scripts/canary-rollout.sh --module network --from v1.4.3 --to v2.0.0 --consumers-file consumers-30d.csv

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep MAJOR notice at 90 days for now — customers still need runway for onprem.
- Consider adding a "compatibility shim" policy for output renames to reduce churn.
- Talk to Maya about making registry-bot attach migration PRs automatically when consumers are detected.

End of draft. Please add comments inline or ping owners for edits.
